name: Abusing GPO Permissions — Attack, Detection & Honeypot
description: Group Policy Objects can be weaponized if non-admin accounts have modification rights. An attacker with GPO write access can push malicious configurations (scheduled tasks, registry keys, immediate tasks) to all computers in the linked OU — including DCs. Detection: Event 5136 (DS Object Modified) for GPO container in AD. Honeypot: monitor 5136 on decoy GPO and immediately disable the modifying account.
notes:
=== BACKGROUND ===
  GPOs define computer and user settings deployed across the domain
  Default: only Domain Admins and Enterprise Admins can modify GPOs
  Misconfiguration: non-admin accounts granted GenericWrite/WriteDACL/WriteOwner
  Impact: attacker can push malicious scheduled tasks, startup scripts, or registry keys
    to ALL machines in the linked OU — including Domain Controllers

=== ATTACK: Enumerate GPO ACLs ===
# PowerView: find non-DC accounts with GPO write access
. .\PowerView.ps1
Get-DomainGPO | Get-ObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.SecurityIdentifier -ne '<DOMAIN_CONTROLLERS_SID>' }
  → Look for: ActiveDirectoryRights = GenericWrite, WriteDACL, or WriteOwner
  → These accounts can modify GPO settings

# Map which OUs the dangerous GPO is linked to
Get-DomainOU | Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericWrite'}

=== ATTACK: Abuse GPO Permissions ===
# Using PowerGPOAbuse or SharpGPOAbuse to add a scheduled task via GPO
# (conceptual — actual command depends on tool used)
# The attack creates an Immediate Task that runs as SYSTEM
# Example: add local admin, execute payload, modify firewall rules

=== DETECTION ===
Event 5136: 'A directory service object was modified'
  → Generated when any AD object attribute is modified
  → For GPO abuse: look for changes to CN={GPO-GUID},CN=POLICIES,CN=SYSTEM,DC=<DOMAIN>
  → The event shows: who modified (Account Name), which object (DN), which attribute
  → Alert when non-DC / non-DA account modifies any GPO CN

Event 4725: 'A user account was disabled'
  → Generated by the honeypot response script when the abuser account is disabled

=== HONEYPOT: PowerShell Monitor Script ===
# Run as scheduled task on DC — monitors Event 5136 for specific GPO modification
# Replace <GPO_GUID> with the GUID of a decoy/honeypot GPO

$TimeSpan = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(-300)  # Look back 5 minutes

$Logs = Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{
    LogName='Security'
    Id=5136
    StartTime=$TimeSpan
} -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {
    $_.Properties[8].Value -match "CN=\{<GPO_GUID>\},CN=POLICIES,CN=SYSTEM,DC=<DOMAIN_DC_PATH>"
}

if ($Logs) {
    foreach ($log in $Logs) {
        # Disable the account that modified the honeypot GPO
        Disable-ADAccount -Identity $log.Properties[3].Value
        # Properties[3] = Account Name (who made the change)

        # Optional: send alert email, create ticket, etc.
        Write-EventLog -LogName 'Application' -Source 'SecurityHoneypot' \
            -EntryType Warning -EventId 9999 \
            -Message "Honeypot GPO modified by: $($log.Properties[3].Value)"
    }
}

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Audit GPO ACLs regularly with PowerView / ADACLScanner
  → Restrict GPO modify rights to Domain Admins only
  → Enable audit policy: 'Audit Directory Service Changes' (Success + Failure)
  → Monitor 5136 events for ALL GPO containers, not just honeypots

defense.why_it_works: GPOs deploy computer/user settings across the domain and, by default, only Domain/Enterprise Admins may edit them. If a non-admin is granted GenericWrite/WriteDACL/WriteOwner on a GPO, they can push a malicious immediate task, startup script, or registry key to every machine in the linked OU — including DCs.
defense.prerequisites: Write access (GenericWrite/WriteDACL/WriteOwner) on a GPO that is linked to an OU containing target machines.
defense.impact: Code execution as SYSTEM on all computers in the linked OU (local admin, payloads, firewall changes) — up to and including Domain Controllers.
defense.detection: Event 5136 ('A directory service object was modified') for the GPO container CN={GUID},CN=POLICIES,CN=SYSTEM,DC=… — it records who changed it, which object, and which attribute. Alert when a non-DC/non-DA account modifies any GPO. Event 4725 appears when a honeypot script disables the abuser.
defense.artifacts: 5136 events on GPO containers from unexpected principals; new Immediate Task / script entries in the GPO's SYSVOL folder; a honeypot decoy GPO firing 5136 on any modification.
defense.prevention: Audit GPO ACLs regularly (PowerView / ADACLScanner); restrict GPO modify rights to Domain Admins; enable 'Audit Directory Service Changes' (Success + Failure); monitor 5136 for ALL GPO containers, not just decoys.
defense.misconfiguration: Group Policy Objects (GPOs) are linked to OUs containing domain computers and users, but non-admin accounts have been granted CreateChild, WriteProperty, or GenericAll rights on those GPOs or the OUs they're linked to. An attacker with GPO write access can push immediate configuration changes to all machines in the scope — including adding themselves to local admins, deploying startup scripts, or disabling AV.
defense.secure_config:
# Remove edit rights from non-admin accounts:
# Group Policy Management Console (GPMC):
# GPO -> Delegation tab -> Remove non-admin entries or change to Read-only

# PowerShell — enumerate and review:
Get-GPPermissions -Guid <gpo-guid> -All
# Remove write access:
Set-GPPermissions -Guid <gpo-guid> -TargetName 'helpdesk' \
    -TargetType Group -PermissionLevel GpoRead

# Alert on GPO changes:
# Event 5136 (Directory Service Object Modified) with objectClass = groupPolicyContainer
# Event 4657 (Registry value modified) after GPO applies
# Microsoft Defender for Identity: 'Suspicious GPO modification' alert
defense.evasion: Revert the GPO change after it executes; scope the malicious setting to one OU; time it around a normal gpupdate window.
